title: Axiom-Hash Bloom Filters: Asymptotic Complexity, Invariant Preservation, and Ruby Implementation
topic: Bloom Filter with Chronos-Hash Hash Functions
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Bloom filters provide a compact probabilistic representation of a set, yet the choice of hash functions and the underlying memory layout critically influence both theoretical guarantees and practical performance. We introduce the Axiom-Hash Bloom filter, a Ruby implementation that leverages deterministic, compositional hash functions to achieve predictable bit-set patterns while preserving the classic false-positive bound. We formally prove that the filter maintains a strict bit-set invariant and derive the asymptotic cost of add and query operations as $O(k)$, where $k$ is the number of hash functions. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) yields a mean latency of 1 308 383 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 764 ops/s. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261116_050243_bloom_filter_with_chronos-hash}
